title: Singapore evidence-led copyright triage
source_status: AGC current-version markers and relevant text checked manually; automated provision extraction incomplete. Application requires human review.

category.title: Work categories and separate rights: ss 8–18, 107

qualification.title: Qualifying connections: ss 3, 109–111, 123; international protection requires regulations

exceptions.title: Exceptions and permitted uses: s 152, Part 5

acknowledgment.title: Acknowledgment for news, criticism or review: s 192

app.title: Asia Pacific Publishing v Pioneers & Leaders [2011] SGCA 37 at [107]–[113] (1987 Act)

gyp.title: Global Yellow Pages v Promedia [2017] SGCA 28 at [24]–[30], [35]–[39] (1987 Act)

recordtv.title: RecordTV v MediaCorp [2010] SGCA 43 at [50]–[60] (1987 Act)

questions.prompt: Are the category-specific conditions for protection satisfied?
questions.explanation: For literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works, identify human authorship and original expression, and recording where required. For film copyright, assess s 123; do not import the authorial originality test.
questions.evidence_needed: Creation drafts, identified author or film maker, publication history and the particular protected work.

questions.prompt: Does the work qualify for protection in Singapore?
questions.explanation: Citizenship, residence, making and first publication can matter. Foreign works may qualify through s 3 and international-protection regulations. Selecting Singapore here does not prove this limb.
questions.evidence_needed: Nationality/residence and first-publication evidence; applicable reciprocating-country regulation.

questions.prompt: Was copyright still in force when the alleged act occurred?
questions.explanation: Check work category, creation, author death, publication and transitional provisions. Do not assume a universal 70-year calculation.
questions.evidence_needed: Dated creation, publication and death records, with the relevant term calculation.

questions.prompt: Does the claimant own the relevant right or have standing as exclusive licensee?
questions.explanation: Authorship, employment, commissioning, assignment and the scope of any exclusive licence require separate checks.
questions.evidence_needed: Chain of title, signed assignments, employment/commission contracts or exclusive licence.

questions.prompt: Does the alleged conduct engage an exclusive right for this work category?
questions.explanation: Describe the act and map it to the right: copying, communication, publication of an unpublished work, performance or adaptation as applicable. Artistic works and films have different rights.
questions.evidence_needed: Dated copies, screenshots, URLs or records showing the act and applicable right.

questions.prompt: Was the relevant act done in Singapore?
questions.explanation: Section 146 requires a Singapore act or authorisation of such an act; internet availability alone should not decide location.
questions.evidence_needed: Hosting, distribution, audience and actor-location evidence relevant to the specific act.

questions.prompt: Was the act outside ownership, licence or other permission?
questions.explanation: Check the actor's ownership and the licence scope, dates, territory and conditions. No known licence is not proof that none exists.
questions.evidence_needed: Licences, correspondence, permissions and scope analysis.

questions.prompt: Does evidence support copying from the claimant's work?
questions.explanation: Access plus relevant similarity can support an inference, subject to rebuttal. Access alone and a computed score cannot establish copying.
questions.evidence_needed: Access chronology, source files, common errors or admissions; address independent creation.

questions.prompt: Do the relied-on similarities concern protected expression?
questions.explanation: Exclude mere ideas, facts, methods and commonplace material from the legal comparison. Compilation rights concern original selection or arrangement.
questions.evidence_needed: Identify the exact passages/features and explain the original expression they reproduce.

questions.prompt: Was the whole work or a legally substantial part taken?
questions.explanation: Assess the quality and importance of protected expression taken in relation to the claimant's work. No similarity percentage is a legal threshold.
questions.evidence_needed: Pinpoint the taking and explain its qualitative importance; consider the claimant's work as a whole.

questions.prompt: Is there evidence of independent creation or a common source?
questions.explanation: A positive answer requires review of the copying inference; it does not automatically prove a defence.
questions.evidence_needed: Independent drafts, dates, common-source material and an account of the creation process.

questions.prompt: Has fair use been assessed as applicable?
questions.explanation: Assess all relevant circumstances, including the four s 191 factors, and acknowledgment under s 192 where relevant. The tool records your assessment without balancing the factors itself.
questions.evidence_needed: Complete the fair-use factors and explain your overall assessment.

questions.prompt: Does another permitted use or statutory exception apply?
questions.explanation: Consider the specific conditions of education, research, computational data analysis, library, accessibility, judicial and other applicable permitted uses. A purpose label is insufficient.
questions.evidence_needed: Identify the provision and evidence satisfying every condition; record why alternatives do not apply.
